title: Samenland: A medieval world where growth and citizens are pure functions of time
author: Doener23
selftext:
Hi,

I’ve been building Samenland ([https://samenland.app](https://samenland.app/)), a slow-paced, multiplayer medieval world set in Northern Germany around 1500.

The architecture, code, historical research, sprite assets, and background music (via Gemini) were developed with [Lovable](https://lovable.dev/invite/LN0I260). I made much faster progress once I started using ChatGPT as a prompt assistant connected directly to the GitHub repository. The character animations remain a weak point—that's what I want to tackle next in combination with ChatGPT.

Most persistent multiplayer games rely on an authoritative server tick loop simulating entities and state in memory. I took a different architectural route: the entire living world is a pure deterministic function of time and world seed.

**Core Architecture**: Zero Tick-Based Simulation State as a pure function: state = f(seed, world\_clock, purchases) Town growth stages, housing density, villager routines, animal herds, goods hauling, church feasts, and weather are never stored as mutable game entities. If 60 players watch the same Hanseatic town across different devices, every client computes the exact same villager walking between the granary and the harbor at 14:15 UTC. Towns continue to grow even when nobody is watching, without running background workers.

**Transactional ledger instead of simulation state**: The backend (PostgreSQL with RLS) stores only immutable player decisions: founding coordinates, road pacts, purchase rows, and signed charter decisions. Economic validation (e.g., municipal treasury caps, rank certificates, disaster recovery) is verified via database guards and cryptographic RPC certificates, never by trusting client-side claims.

**2D Canvas**: Instead of WebGL or Three.js, we chose a native HTML5 2D Canvas with sub-pixel depth sorting:

**2:1 dimetric isometric projection**: All standing objects (buildings, figures, animals, carts) are bucketed and rendered in a single per-tile depth pass. Nothing ever clips through a foreground roof.

**Separation of building and terrain**: Building sprites end cleanly at their foundation threshold. Contact shadows and ground blending are computed procedurally at runtime. 16-tile chunk baking: Flat terrain (turf, water, procedural winter snow paths) bakes into offscreen canvases at most once per frame, keeping panning at a steady 60–120 FPS on mobile and desktop. Stack

**Frontend/Fullstack**: React 19, TanStack Start, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4

**Backend**: PostgreSQL (RLS, stored procedure guards, real-time broadcast for ephemeral mayor strolls) 

**License**: MIT

PS: I was not sure about the flair. The game is not commercial, but it's self promotion.
